newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil spuds dry well in Norwegian Sea.
newsitem.headline: Statoil spuds dry well in Norwegian Sea.

text.p: An exploration well in block 6608/8 in the Norwegian Sea found only spore traces of hydrocarbons and was not tested by operator Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil), the Norwegian Oil Directorate (OD) said on Monday.
Statoil is operator of licence 200, which covers blocks 6608/7 and 6608/8, awarded under Norway's 14th concession round in 1993. The well was the first to be spudded under that licence.

"Only spores of hydrocarbons were discovered in the well, but the drilling has, however, given useful information on the geological structure in the exploration area known as Nordland II," the OD said in a statement.
Partners in licence 200 are Statoil with 65 percent -- including 40 percent of the state's direct financial interest -- Phillips Petroleum with 20 percent and Neste Oy with 15 percent.
